chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the prayer on the day of al-Fitr and al-Adha, so he said: "There is no prayer except with the Imam."

Because the intended meaning is that there is no obligatory prayer except with the Imam, and it was not meant by it that there is no prayer whatsoever in all cases, as indicated by what we have previously mentioned, and to clarify that further is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is the Eid prayer considered valid if performed individually without an Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the Eid prayers are considered fully obligatory (fard) only when performed in congregation with the Imam, a nuance derived from the context of the chain of narrators. The text explicitly distinguishes this from a general exclusion of all prayer forms, affirming that while individual prayer is valid, the specific ritual status of Eid prayer is tied to the communal leadership. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam's role in establishing the public manifestation of religious rites.
